chunks: And al-Shaykh—may Allah, Exalted is He, strengthen him—informed me, saying:

Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad informed me from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the Friday ghusl, and he said: “It is obligatory in travel and residence, except that a concession was given to women while traveling due to scarcity of water.” And he said: “The ghusl of janābah is obligatory; the ghusl of the menstruating woman when she becomes pure is obligatory; the ghusl of istiḥāḍah is obligatory if she uses cotton and the blood passes through the cotton, then she must perform ghusl for every two prayers, and for Fajr there is a ghusl. If the blood does not pass through the cotton, then she must perform ghusl once each day and wudu (ablution) for every salat (prayer). The ghusl of the woman in nifās is obligatory; the ghusl of the newborn is obligatory; the ghusl of the dead is obligatory; the ghusl of the one who has washed a dead person is obligatory; the ghusl of the muḥrim is obligatory; the ghusl of the Day of ʿArafah is obligatory; the ghusl for ziyārah is obligatory except in case of illness; the ghusl for entering the House is obligatory; the ghusl for entering the sanctuary is recommended, that one should not enter it except with ghusl; the ghusl of mubāhalah is obligatory; the ghusl for seeking rain is obligatory; the ghusl of the first night of the month of Ramaḍān is recommended; the ghusl of the twenty-first night is sunnah (prophetic tradition); the ghusl of the twenty-third night is sunnah (prophetic tradition), one should not abandon it, because Laylat al-Qadr is hoped for in one of them; the ghusl of the Day of al-Fiṭr and the ghusl of the Day of al-Aḍḥā are sunnah (prophetic tradition), I do not like their being abandoned; and the ghusl of istikhārah is recommended.”

So this hadith includes, by the apparent wording, the obligation of the six ghusls mentioned earlier. No one may say that you cannot cite this report as evidence because it includes mention of the obligation of ghusls regarding which you have agreed that they are not obligatory. For if we were left with the apparent wording of the report, we would say that all these ghusls are obligatory; however, reports clarifying these ghusls and that they are not obligatory have prevented us from that. So when these reports are established, we interpret what this report contains of the wording of obligation as meaning the emphasis of the sunnah (prophetic tradition), and we shall present later what indicates that, if Allah, Exalted is He, wills.

key_terms.السُّنَّةِ: an emphasized prescribed practice, not necessarily strict obligation in this context
key_terms.الِاسْتِحَاضَةِ: irregular bleeding that carries specific purity rulings
key_terms.غُسْلُ الزِّيَارَةِ: the ritual bath performed for ziyārah
key_terms.غُسْلُ الْجَنَابَةِ: the ritual bath required after janābah
key_terms.لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ: the Night of Decree sought among the specified nights

ai.seo_question: Which ghusls are described as obligatory or recommended in this hadith from Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses numerous forms of ghusl and presents their rulings, beginning with the Friday ghusl and extending to ghusls related to ritual impurity, worship, sacred occasions, and special acts. The closing passage explains that although the apparent wording indicates obligation for many of them, other reports clarify that some instances express emphatic sunnah (prophetic tradition) rather than strict obligation.
